question: Does adding `group_carriage` to collective_groups.enabled_domains change WHEN the person-004 -> person-000 social_request_help interaction is accepted (698 vs 699)?
method: Reused build_genesis/run_tick exactly as backend/tools/_probe_8b_carriage.py. Read-only; no simulation code modified. Step 1: ran the current committed pipeline (group_carriage enabled, as currently present -- uncommitted -- in scenarios/collective_groups.py). Step 2: temporarily removed "group_carriage" from collective_groups.enabled_domains, re-ran the identical 1000-tick probe, then restored the file to its exact prior (uncommitted) content.

STEP_1_current_pipeline_group_carriage_e.result: Exactly ONE social_request_help event from person-004 to person-000 exists in the whole 1000-tick run. It is accepted at TICK 698, id `evt-698-13861-115d344e`.

adjacent_context_evt_699.note: This is the group_carriage domain's own transmission-detection proposal, committed one tick after the qualifying action (698) per its documented one-tick observation lag (see domains/group_carriage_contracts.py module docstring: 'a qualifying social action accepted at tick T is detected and turned into a transmission event at T+1'). This explains why the carrier record's via_event_id cites evt-698-... while its own learned_tick is 699 -- that field pair is internally consistent and NOT itself a bug.

GROUND_TRUTH.label: VERIFIED
GROUND_TRUTH.statement: There is exactly ONE person-004 -> person-000 social_request_help event in the run (not two). Its accepted tick is NOT invariant to enabling group_carriage: it is tick 699 when group_carriage is disabled (matching the earlier probe_8b_carriage_1000.json evidence, and matching HEAD's committed enabled_domains list) and tick 698 when group_carriage is enabled (matching the current probe_8b_carriage_registry_state_1000.json via_event_id evidence, evt-698-13861-115d344e). The event_id tick-698 in the carrier record's via_event_id is therefore ground truth for the underlying action's accepted tick IN THE group_carriage-ENABLED CONFIGURATION -- but that configuration itself produces a different action-acceptance tick than the group_carriage-DISABLED configuration for this same actor/action. The earlier probe's tick=699 recording was not a probe bug; it reflects a genuinely different trajectory for the group_carriage-disabled run.

ACCEPTED_EVENT_COUNT_COMPARISON_690_702.label: VERIFIED
ACCEPTED_EVENT_COUNT_COMPARISON_690_702.observation: Ticks 690-697 (8 ticks) have byte-identical accepted-event counts between the two configurations. Divergence first appears at tick 698 (18 vs 17 -- the shifted social_request_help event) and reappears at tick 702 (21 vs 20, a further downstream divergence not explained by the single shifted event alone, evidencing the trajectories continue to differ after tick 698 rather than re-converging).

MECHANISM_IDENTIFIED.label: VERIFIED (code-level) / LIKELY (as the specific causal chain for this exact tick shift)
MECHANISM_IDENTIFIED.root_cause: backend/domains/living_settlement_domain.py:_apply_group_norm_influence (lines ~183-236) is a Stage 8B Leg 1 hook, already present and wired into candidate scoring (called at line 553: `candidates = _apply_group_norm_influence(candidates, entity_id, frame.entities, tick)`), that boosts REPAIR_SHELTER candidate scores for any person who is a CARRIER (per group-carriage-000) of a live shelter_upkeep_norm targeting that shelter. Per its own docstring: 'Inert when no valid group-norm registry OR no valid group-carriage registry exists (e.g. the living_settlement scenario, or group_carriage not enabled) ... with no carriage registry, no one is ever eligible, so the nudge never fires.' This is confirmed by code reading, not simulation: `carriage_registry = entities.get(GROUP_CARRIAGE_REGISTRY_ID); carriers = (...) if isinstance(carriage_registry, dict) and carriage_registry.get('schema_version') == GROUP_CARRIAGE_REGISTRY_VERSION else {}` -- with group_carriage disabled, GROUP_CARRIAGE_REGISTRY_ID never exists in entities, so `carriers` is always `{}` and the function returns candidates unmodified for everyone, every tick.
MECHANISM_IDENTIFIED.activation_evidence: Per memory/evidence/stage-8b-leg1/probe_8b_carriage_1000.json (adoption_samples), person-004 is the sole non-supporter in EVERY observed group-goal adoption (person-004 never appears as a formation-backfill carrier for any norm). Per probe_8b_carriage_registry_state_1000.json, the other 7 members (person-000,001,002,003,005,006,007) were formation-backfilled as carriers of group-norm-5ae28cfdb0f88c3addd5 at learned_tick=684 -- well before the tick-690-702 observation window. Therefore: when group_carriage is enabled, `_apply_group_norm_influence` becomes active for those 7 carriers starting shortly after tick 684, boosting their REPAIR_SHELTER candidates for the remainder of the run (subject to the urgent-survival suppression check). This alters their action selection across ticks 685-698, which -- because all agents read shared, mutually-observable world state (positions, resource levels, pressures) each tick -- cascades into a measurably different world trajectory by tick 698, which is exactly where the accepted-event-count divergence in this probe first appears. Person-004 itself only becomes a carrier THROUGH the tick-698/699 transmission event, so the influence cannot be acting on person-004's OWN candidates before that tick; the shift is attributed to the other 7 carriers' altered behaviour perturbing the shared camp state that person-004's own decision logic reads.
MECHANISM_IDENTIFIED.classification: This is a DOCUMENTED, INTENTIONAL cross-domain influence pathway (CLAUDE.md invariant 6: 'Influence is read-only, member/carrier-grounded, boosts/suppresses only existing candidates, never outranks urgent survival'), not a hidden bug, not RNG-stream leakage (core/rng.py uses per-(seed,name) named streams specifically to prevent call-order-dependent draw shifting -- confirmed by reading core/rng.py; this mechanism instead operates purely through score-boost-driven candidate selection, which is expected to alter concrete action timing). It IS a real, measured, non-trivial change to the simulation's tick-by-tick trajectory caused solely by enabling a domain advertised as 'proposal-only' and writing only its own new registry (group-carriage-000): enabling group_carriage does not just add new registry-write events, it also ACTIVATES a pre-existing, previously-fully-inert influence hook in an unrelated domain (living_settlement_domain.py) that changes AGENT ACTION SELECTION for members unrelated to group_carriage's own registry writes. No deeper trace of the exact per-tick candidate-score chain from tick 684 to 698 was performed (would require additional multi-tick candidate-score instrumentation beyond this probe's scope); the code-level activation gate and the tick-684 pre-window backfill timing are the decisive, measured evidence for this classification.
